 Order

The petitioner/A2 in C.C.No.1807 of 2018 facing trial for the offence under Section 420 and 506(i)
IPC filed a discharge petition in Crl.M.P.No.6594 of 2018 on the file of the learned V Metropolitan Magistrate, Egmore, Chennai and the same was dismissed by order dated 02.07.2024.
Against which, the present criminal revision petition is filed.
2.The defacto complainant/L.W.1 lodged a complaint with the respondent police and a case in Crime No.36 of 2017 registered on 04.01.2017 for the offence under Sections 420 and 506(i) IPC.
The complaint was lodged against A1/Gokulnath alone.

Thereafter, on completion of investigation,
charge sheet filed on 28.07.2017 arraying Gokulnath as single accused in the case listing nine witnesses.
Thereafter, charge sheet returned to include the petitioner as accused.
The learned Magistrate took cognizance against the petitioner arraying her as A2.
The petitioner is the divorced wife of A1/Gokulnath.
3 . T h e g i s t o f t h e c a s e i s t h a t t h e d e f a c t o c o m p l a i n a n t a n d h e r h u s b a n d https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
Ganesh got married in the year 2007, they have no issues and for that reason, they got separated in the year 2015.
Thereafter, the said Gokulnath came in contact and became friendly with the defacto complainant through facebook and they were in a live-in relationship, living in Bangalore.

The said Gokulnath claimed that he divorced his wife/petitioner herein, believing the same the defacto complainant continued her relationship with him and during that time, she spent huge money for Gokulnath.

Later, defacto complainant came to know that the said Gokulnath was parallely maintaining his relationship with the petitioner and further finding Gokulnath having relationship with other women, the defacto complainant moved away from him and got separated.
The said Gokulnath forcing the defacto complainant to continue relationship with him, which was resisted by the defacto complainant thereafter there was abuse and threat.
The said Gokulnath threatened the defacto complainant to post the intimate photographs taken between them in social media and he also demanded Rs.10 lakhs if she part way.

As regards the petitioner,
she is said to have called L.W.2/Ganesh, estranged husband of the defacto complainant and threatened him that she would post the intimate photos of the defacto complainant and Gokulnath if he fails to pay Rs.5 lakhs.
The respondent https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis police on registration of the case, enquired the witnesses and filed charge sheet listing L.W.1 to L.W.11.
4.The contention of the learned counsel for the petitioner is that the case itself is highly artificial.

The case projected is that during the period 01.12.2015 to 31.08.2016, the said Gokulnath and the defacto complainant were living together in Bangalore and at that time, she spent huge money to Gokulnath on the belief he divorced his wife/petitioner herein and defacto complainant continued her relationship with him.
This might be a case against the said Gokulnath for making such statements, but not against the petitioner.
Further, nowhere from any of the statement, it is seen the petitioner made any such claim or statement to anyone.
It is not the case that the defacto complainant at any point contacted or verified with the petitioner on the claim made by Gokulnath.
In fact, the petitioner obtained divorce from the said Gokulnath on 12.08.2021 by mutual consent finding that he is an untrusty person with shadowing character.

2 charge sheet are L.W.3, a driver who normally shuttles the defacto complainant and A1/Gokulnath,
L.W.4/friend of defacto complainant who deposited some money in the account of A1 at the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis instruction of the defacto complainant, L.W.5, a co-tenant in Bangalore where the defacto complainant and the said Gokulnath lived together, L.W.6 and L.W.7 are the witnesses for observation mahazar and rough sketch, L.W.8 and L.W.9 are the witnesses for arrest and confession of A1/Gokulnath, L.W.10 is the Sub-Inspector of Police who registered a case and arrested the said Gokulnath and L.W.11 filed the charge sheet.

None of the witnesses except for L.W.1 and L.W.2 state that the petitioner demanded Rs.5 lakhs, otherwise intimate photographs of the defacto complainant and A1/Gokulnath would be posted in social media.
The petitioner already had a strained relationship with the said Gokulnath, living separately and obtained divorce.
In view of the same, taking the statement to be true, then no case is made out.
Admittedly, as regards the case of cheating it is projected against A1.

This petitioner is said to have threatened L.W.2 and if the statement is taken to be true, mere threat would not be sufficient in absence of any action which is a settled principle and proposition of law reiterated by this Court as well as the Apex Court.

5.The learned Additional Public Prosecutor on the other hand submitted that on the complaint of the defacto complainant, a case in Crime https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis No.36 of 2017 registered on 04.01.2017 for the offence under Sections 420 and 506(i) IPC and on completion of investigation,
charge sheet filed.

A1 and A2 are husband and wife, both of them joined together, threatened the defacto complainant and her estranged husband/L.W.2, demanded ransom of Rs.10 lakhs and Rs.5 lakhs further if the money is not paid, some intimate photographs of the defacto complainant and A1/Gokulnath will be posted in the social media.
The ground raised by the petitioner is factual in nature, it has to be decided during trial and not at this stage.

He fairly submitted that complaint was lodged only against Gokulnath and after completion of investigation, initially charge sheet filed against the said Gokulnath before the Lower Court on 28.07.2017, thereafter the Magistrate returned the charge sheet, directing to include the petitioner as A2 in this case and thereafter,
A2/petitioner has arrayed as accused.

He further submitted that except for a stain statement of LW1 and LW2, there is no other material against the petitioner.
6.Considering the submissions made and on perusal of the materials

, it is not in dispute that the defacto complainant and A1/Gokulnath became friendly through social media and they were living together in Bangalore for https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis some time, during that time, the defacto complainant spent huge money for Gokulnath but there is nothing to show that the defacto complainant spent even a single penny on deception or false representation given by the petitioner herein.
It is nowhere seen that the petitioner and the defacto complainant or L.W.2/Ganesh had any contact during the relevant period.
The only allegation against the petitioner is that she had contacted, threatened both L.W.1 and L.W.2, it is only an empty threat if taken to be true.
It is further seen that none of the witnesses spoken anything about the petitioner in any manner.
It is admitted by the defacto complainant that already the defacto complainant got separated from L.W.2 in the year 2015 and they were living separately by mutual consent.
The petitioner obtained divorce by mutual consent on 12.08.2021 in I.D.O.P.No.1827 of 2020 on the file of the V Additional Family Court, Chennai.
The relationship between the petitioner and A1/Gokulnath was not cordial, it is a strained relationship and finally ended in divorce.
It is also seen that charge sheet initially filed against A1 alone which was returned by the learned Magistrate and thereafter, A2/petitioner name Sugany @ Suganya Caylist vs State Rep.

3 arrayed as accused and final report filed.
Except for this cosmetic change, no justifiable reason given.
The allegation is that the petitioner threatened to post some photographs https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis available in the petitioner's laptop which would be exposed and circulated.
There is no seizure of any laptop or any photographs from the petitioner to confirm that the threat was real and imminent.
In the absence of any seizure or any material, merely on the empty words charge sheet cannot be filed and no charges can be framed without any materials.
Thus, in view of the same, this Court is inclined to discharge the petitioner.
Accordingly, the order passed by the learned V Metropolitan Magistrate, Egmore, Chennai.
In Crl.M.P.No.6594 of 2018 dated 02.07.2024 is set aside and the petitioner is discharged from the case in C.C.No.1807 of 2018 on the file of the learned V Metropolitan Magistrate, Egmore, Chennai.
7.In the result, the criminal revision petition stands allowed.
Consequently, connected miscellaneous petitions are closed.
